subject: Commencement: Northstar VPC connectivity intake & access matrix
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@northstar-health.com>; procurement@northstar-health.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commencement: Northstar VPC connectivity intake & access matrix

Hi Eric / Northstar team —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. To kick off the VPC/on-prem intake we need a quick pass on connectivity, ACLs, and the environment access matrix so we can schedule the provisioning window and SRE handoff. I attached a prefilled intake template (northstar-intake-template.xlsx) to speed this up.

Immediate asks (please reply inline):
- Confirm the target VPC/Peering model: (VPC peering / Cloud Interconnect / Transit Gateway) and who owns the routing (Northstar netops vs. cloud infra).
- Egress policy: are outbound internet egress allowed, or must all external requests go through a customer-managed NAT/proxy?
- KMS/HSM: will you provide key material (BYOK) via KMS? If so, share the KMS ARN and initial key admin list.
- Syslog/Monitoring: endpoint(s) for syslog and metrics (host:port) and any TLS requirements.
- Service account & firewall: list of IP ranges we should allow (Redwood egress ranges included in attachment) and service account principals we should provision.
- Maintenance windows and blackout periods for the first 30 days.

Attachment: northstar-intake-template.xlsx — please use tab "Network + Access" and return by EOD Wednesday to keep the current provisioning date.

I'll schedule a 30-min technical intake once we have the template back; Dev will lead the technical run-down.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Commencement: Northstar VPC connectivity intake & access matrix

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear list. We've filled most of the Network + Access tab and attached it to this reply (see northstar-intake-template.xlsx updated). Key notes:
- We'll use a Cloud Interconnect with route exchange handled by our NetOps team (they own route tables).
- Egress must go via our corporate proxy (no direct internet egress). We'll provide proxy host/port and a TLS cert.
- KMS: we will provide a customer-managed key in AWS KMS (arn: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01). Key admins are myself and Jenna Park (netops).
- Syslog: logs.forwarding.northstar-health.net:6514 (TLS required).
- IPs: added the allowed CIDR ranges in the spreadsheet.
- Maintenance: prefer Tuesday/Thursday 01:00-05:00 UTC for non-business-impacting changes.

Procurement: we are ready to issue a PO once we have final pricing and an updated SOW.

I'll be available for the intake call Thursday morning (10/08) between 09:00–11:00 PT.

—Eric
Eric Barnes
Director, Cloud Infrastructure — Northstar Health

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@northstar-health.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commencement: Northstar VPC connectivity intake & access matrix

Thanks Eric — great, that gives us what we need to start designing the connector. A few technical follow-ups from the template:

1) Interconnect details — can you confirm the ASN and whether you will accept static routes or prefer BGP? If BGP, do you want MD5 authentication?

2) Proxy TLS termination — will the corporate proxy present a cert signed by a public CA, or should we be prepared to pin an internal CA root? If internal, we'll need the CA bundle.

3) KMS key policy — please add Redwood service principal (redwood-kms@redwood-service) as an encrypted-data key user with Encrypt/Decrypt and Describe permissions; we can provide the exact IAM policy if you prefer.

4) CIDR overlap — I noticed one of the allowed ranges overlaps with Redwood default service ranges; we will propose a NAT translation for the conflict if you cannot change the CIDR.

5) Egress flow — because outbound must go through your proxy, we will route all external model downloads and telemetry through that path; this will increase initial token latency slightly during large model pull operations — we can cache layers in the enclave to mitigate.

I've attached a short integration guide (redwood-connector-guide.pdf) that outlines the expected ports and IPs. If you can confirm items 1–3 before the intake call, we'll be able to present a concrete runbook during the meeting.

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-08T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commencement: Northstar VPC connectivity intake & access matrix

Adding SRE acceptance criteria so Northstar has visibility:

- Connectivity verification: SRE will run active TCP health checks to the model-serving enclave on the allowed ports for 72 hours.
- Metrics & traces: please ensure that Prometheus/OTLP endpoints are reachable over TLS from Redwood egress IPs.
- Backup & restore: initial snapshot policy is daily; we need an S3-compatible endpoint (or presigned URLs) and the retention policy.
- Incident comms: provide a primary and secondary PagerDuty escalation contact for the first 30 days.
- SLA exceptions: if any of the above require design changes (e.g., forced zero-egress), flag them now so we can scope expected performance delta.

I'll prepare a short checklist we can use during the intake call.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
